basic_details.job_title: NeGD Non-Technical Intern Recruitment 2026 – Apply Online for 12 Posts
basic_details.short_information: The National e-Governance Division (NeGD), Digital India Corporation (DIC), Ministry of Electronics & Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India, has invited applications for 12 non-technical interns under its Winter Programme 2026. The token remuneration is Rs. 15,000 per month. The minimum duration is two months, extendable by up to one month. Eligible students apply through the online application form, sponsored or forwarded by their institution, by 20 November 2026 (Friday).

content_sections.heading: About NeGD
content_sections.text: The notice is issued by the National e-Governance Division (NeGD) of Digital India Corporation (DIC) under the Ministry of Electronics & Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India. The Internship Programme is conducted twice a year, as a Summer Internship Programme and a Winter Internship Programme. This notice covers the Winter Programme 2026.

content_sections.heading: Vacancy Details
content_sections.text: NeGD has listed 12 intern positions in five interest areas: 5 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 1 = 12. Each area contains one or more roles, described under Job Description below.

rows.roles: 1. Policy, Documentation Support & Monitoring & Reporting; 2. Strategic Planning Activities; 3. Data Analytics; 4. Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning
5. Content Writing, Design & Visual Content Support; 6. Campaigns research, Events & Outreach Support
7. Training Programs support, Content & Curriculum Assistance; 8. Event Management & Logistics; 9. Data Privacy & Securities; 10. Internet of Things / New & Emerging Technologies / Cloud Computing

content_sections.heading: Who Can Apply
content_sections.text: The qualification below applies to the non-technical internship as a whole. The notice does not name a separate qualification for each interest area. Eligible applicants are students from recognised universities in India who meet any one of these conditions: They have secured at least 60% marks in the last held degree or certificate examination and have completed education under the 10+2+3 pattern, that is, 15 years of formal education; OR They are pursuing the pre-final or final year of Engineering in the 10+2+4 pattern of education; OR They are pursuing the pre-final or final year of a Diploma/Certificate course; OR They are pursuing the pre-final or final year of an integrated degree course or dual degree of the 10+2+5 pattern of education. For the discipline-specific eligibility of each role, candidates should refer to the official notification.

content_sections.heading: Pay and Tenure
content_sections.text: A token remuneration of Rs. 15,000/- per month is paid to an intern, subject to satisfactory performance duly certified by the Mentor. It is paid after the complete tenure of the internship, on submission of a Report duly accepted by NeGD. The notice prints no HRA or other allowance. The minimum duration of the internship is two months, extendable up to one month (total three months), depending on the candidate's performance, NeGD's requirements and the time the intern is willing to spend with NeGD. Every batch of interns or individual interns has a Mentor from NeGD, preferably the HOD of the Division/Project. NeGD issues certificates on completion of the internship and submission of the Report, duly countersigned and accepted by the Competent Authority.

content_sections.heading: NeGD Recruitment 2026 Job Description
content_sections.text: The duties below are printed in the notice for each role. They are grouped by interest area. 1. Policy, Documentation Support & Monitoring & Reporting Assist in preparing Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), BRDs, policy analysis documents / GAP analysis, and help in maintaining and updating project status trackers or documentation repositories. Track KPIs, milestones, or progress of projects. Support in drafting weekly / monthly status reports. Update dashboards or monitoring tools (Excel / Google Sheets). Prepare briefs / concept notes. 2. Strategic Planning Activities Contribute to research, background material, and benchmarking to support planning for new programmes. Summarize policies, case studies, and initiatives for internal references. Conduct research on similar digital transformation programmes across sectors or geographies. Compile learnings that could inform strategy or implementation. Assist in tracking programme-level compliance with timelines, budget reporting, or deliverables, and help prepare input for periodic reports or audits. 3. Data Analytics Assist in curating and organizing datasets, helping ensure data is clean, well-labelled, and ready for analysis. KPI defining, drafting case studies, data success stories, or visual summaries of findings for broader communication. Conducting secondary research on data use in governance, such as how other countries use analytics in public service delivery, and compiling best practices for internal learning. 4. Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning Automated KPI tracking and dashboard updates and pattern recognition to detect performance trends. Smart document search and tagging using Natural Learning Processing (NLP) for templates, reports, and past cases. To identify unusual delays or dropouts in activities. Use AI to review internal documents for clarity, redundancy, or outdated content. 5. Content Writing, Design & Visual Content Support Draft social media posts, captions, or threads for platforms like Twitter, LinkedIn, Facebook. Write blogs, articles, and newsletters related to Digital India, government digital services, or success stories. Help prepare press releases, media briefs, or content for campaigns. Use tools like Canva, PowerPoint, or Photoshop to create posters & banners. 6. Campaigns research, Events & Outreach Support Research target audiences, channels, and key messaging strategies. Help brainstorm creative ideas for future campaigns or social media strategies. Support logistics and planning for outreach events, conferences, and exhibitions. Draft event invites, agendas, anchor scripts, and speaker notes. Help with registration, feedback collection, or post-event reporting. 7. Training Programs support, Content & Curriculum Assistance Help review or proofread training materials, presentations, or case studies. Organize or maintain learning content libraries (videos, PDFs, slide decks). Assist in structuring online courses on platforms like iGOT or LMS portals. 8

content_sections.heading: How to Apply for NeGD Recruitment 2026
content_sections.text: For general guidelines, the notice refers applicants to the Internship Policy on NeGD's website, https://negd.gov.in/ . The notice names no documents to be attached.

content_sections.heading: Selection and Interview
content_sections.text: Interns are shortlisted based on marks in the qualifying degree. They are selected for the internship through interviews, or based on the judgement of the internal selection committee, as per NeGD's requirements. Weightage is given to the top 100 colleges per year, as per the ranking of the National Institutional Ranking Framework by the Ministry of Education. The selection of the candidate is based on the prescribed weightage formula. The notice does not print the weightage formula or the interview mode.

content_sections.heading: Important Dates
content_sections.text: Only the last date is printed as a fixed date. The rest of the calendar is described as tentative by NeGD.

faq.question: Q1. How many intern positions are available in the NeGD Winter Internship 2026?
faq.answer: The notice lists 12 intern positions: 5 in Programme Management, 2 each in Awareness and Communication, Capacity Building and Technology Management, and 1 in Project Appraisal.

faq.question: Q2. What is the last date to apply for the NeGD non-technical internship?
faq.answer: The last date for submission of the Internship Application Form is 20 November 2026 (Friday).

faq.question: Q3. What is the qualification for the NeGD internship?
faq.answer: Students need at least 60% marks in the last held degree or certificate examination under the 10+2+3 pattern (15 years of formal education). Students pursuing the pre-final or final year of Engineering (10+2+4), a Diploma/Certificate course, or an integrated or dual degree (10+2+5) are also eligible.

faq.question: Q4. How much remuneration does a NeGD intern get?
faq.answer: A token remuneration of Rs. 15,000/- per month is paid, subject to satisfactory performance certified by the Mentor. It is paid after the complete tenure and submission of an accepted Report.

faq.question: Q5. How do I apply for the NeGD internship?
faq.answer: Submit the prescribed online application form by 20 November 2026. The application must be sponsored or forwarded by the institution where you are enrolled or have recently passed out.

faq.question: Q6. How are NeGD interns selected?
faq.answer: Interns are shortlisted on marks in the qualifying degree. They are selected through interviews or by the internal selection committee's judgement, using the prescribed weightage formula, with weightage to the top 100 NIRF-ranked colleges.

faq.question: Q7. How long is the NeGD internship?
faq.answer: The minimum duration is two months, extendable by up to one month (total three months). The tentative internship period is December to February, with extension up to March.

faq.question: Q8. Does meeting the minimum qualification guarantee an internship at NeGD?
faq.answer: No. Candidates with exposure in the intended internship, a good academic background and higher qualifications based on need are given preference.

faq.question: Q9. Can the qualification be relaxed for the NeGD internship?
faq.answer: Yes, it may be relaxed in deserving cases based on NeGD's need, with prior approval of the Competent Authority.

faq.question: Q10. When will selected candidates be informed?
faq.answer: The tentative calendar shows selection in the last week of November and intimation of selection to colleges or candidates in the 1st week of December.
